sentences.text: Whether the plaintiff is entitled to a decree for recovery of Rs.7,83,562/- from the defendant?
OPP Plaintiff, in the present case, is the husband of defendant.
Defendant had filed a complaint against the plaintiff under various sections of IPC including 498A.
While granting bail Hon'ble High Court of Delhi had directed plaintiff to pay defendant an amount of Rs.1 lakh as interim measure.
Prior to this, plaintiff had also paid an amount of Rs.60,000/- to the defendant before the Ld. Sessions Court, when his bail application was dismissed.
CS DJ 428/2018 Ajai Vatan(Sr.Citizen )Vs. Shashi Bala Aneja Page 6of 12

Plaintiff's suit is based on the premise that whatever money he had given in pursuance of the orders passed by the Ld Sessions Court and Hon'ble High Court of Delhi deserves to be refunded to him as he was acquitted in the criminal case which formed the subject matter of both the bail applications.

In substance, what plaintiff is asserting is that whatever money was given by him to the defendant now constitutes a financial liability on defendant towards the Plaintiff that needs to be discharged.
It is a settled position of law that a husband is duty bound to maintain his wife.

It has been time and again held by various High Courts and Hon'ble Supreme Court of India that maintenance is neither a charity nor a luxury rather it is a measure intended to protect women from vagrancy and destitution.

Hence, legally speaking if any money is paid by a husband to his wife, unless contrary is shown, it will always be presumed that it was towards maintenance and therefore, there cannot be any automatic right to refund.
In the present case, whatever money was given by the plaintiff to his wife

,
can either be interim maintenance or a pre-condition to the bail.
Plaintiff in his evidence has produced two orders passed by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi.
On the request of the petitioner, adjourned to October 31, 2008.

Plaintiff in para no.12 of his plaint has stated that order dated 31.10.2008 of the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi implies that if defendant ultimately loses her criminal complaint, she will have to return the amount of Rs.1,60,000/- which was given by him before Patiala House Courts as well as before Hon'ble High Court of Delhi.
Plaintiff in his cross examination reiterated that he had paid Rs.1,00,000/- to the defendant on the directions of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi.

Upon being asked that the order dated 31.10.2008 nowhere reflects his entitlement to seek refund, he has stated that there was clear and categorical direction of the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi that said Rs.1,00,000/- was being paid to the complainant without prejudice to the rights and contentions of the plaintiff.
I have perused the evidence on the record and have also deliberated on the position of law in this regard.
The order passed by the Hon'ble High Court nowhere gives plaintiff any liberty to seek refund, in case the FIR and the consequent trial results in his acquittal.
Hon'ble High Court by the order has merely dealt with the plaintiff's right to defend himself in case the chargesheet is filed and the matter goes to trial.
As the money has been paid in pursuance of the order passed by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi, it can only be refunded upon the specific directions of the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi itself.
The inception of the suit itself is premised on erroneous interpretation of High Court's order.
The money, if it was given as an interim maintenance to the wife, is not recoverable.

If the same was given as a pre-condition to the bail then also the money CS DJ 428/2018 Ajai Vatan(Sr.Citizen )Vs.
Shashi Bala Aneja Page 10of 12 is not recoverable as plaintiff has already received an order on the basis of it.

sentences.text: This court is of the considered opinion that the amount given by the plaintiff to the defendant cannot be recovered for several reasons which are summarized herein below:-
(i) The amount of Rs.1,00,000/- was paid voluntarily by the plaintiff in order to secure the benefit of bail.

And Rs.60,000/-
were paid in lieu of the jewellery of the defendant.
Both these payments were taken into consideration by Hon'ble High Court while granting bail to the plaintiff (as reflected in orders dated 20.11.2007 and 31.10.2008).
Once he accepted and acted upon the condition he cannot later undo a judicial order unless the order itself, is set aside.
(ii) Bail order has attained finality as it was never challenged.
(iii) There were no express directions given by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi stipulating that the said amount will be refunded in case, the criminal case fails.
There is no automatic refund in such cases.
(iv) The usage of word 'without prejudice' by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi was only with respect to the contention that he may raise in the criminal matter in case chargesheet is filed.
However, the plaintiff is reading the order as 'without prejudice to plaintiff's right to receive refund, in case he is acquitted'.
It is clearly not the case.
(v) The money has been paid in pursuance of the order passed by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi.

A district court can never direct refund of such an amount unless Hon'ble High Court itself passes specific directions to the plaintiff to seek refund by filing CS DJ 428/2018 Ajai Vatan(Sr.Citizen )Vs.

Shashi Bala Aneja Page 11of 12 a suit.
In view of the above discussion, plaintiff is not entitled to any relief.
The suit of the plaintiff is accordingly dismissed.
